Key Factors Accelerating Growth in AI for Orthopedic Surgery The rising prevalence of musculoskeletal disorders (MSK) is a primary factor driving growth in the AI orthopedic surgery market. These disorders encompass injuries or chronic conditions affecting muscles, bones, joints, tendons, or ligaments, often leading to pain and restricted movement. Increasing sedentary lifestyles contribute to this rise, causing muscle weakening and joint stress. AI enhances management of MSK conditions through early and accurate diagnosis using sophisticated image analysis and data interpretation. It also supports personalized treatment planning and outcome predictions, ultimately improving patient recovery.

Real-World Data Supporting Growth in AI Orthopedics For example, in January 2024, the UK’s Office for Health Improvement and Disparities reported that 18.4% of individuals aged 16 and older had a long-term musculoskeletal condition in 2023, up from 17.6% in 2022. This upward trend in MSK disorders underpins the increasing adoption of AI technologies in orthopedic surgery, as healthcare providers seek more effective ways to address these widespread conditions.
